name: Reformism
summary: Reformism holds that capitalist society can be transformed, or at least made far more just, by gradual change through existing democratic institutions rather than revolution. In its classic socialist form (Bernstein's evolutionary socialism) universal suffrage, trade unions, cooperatives and municipal enterprise are the levers; in its later social-democratic form it stresses welfare, regulation and Keynesian management of a mixed economy. It rejects collapse theories, the dictatorship of the proletariat and vanguard politics.
scope: Reformist socialism as Eduard Bernstein set it out in Evolutionary Socialism (1899): the labour movement should pursue socialism by lawful, gradual democratic change instead of revolution or a collapse of capitalism. The Marxists Internet Archive glossary defines reformism as the workers'-movement current aiming at change by the gradual accumulation of small changes, and names Bernstein as its representative. It excludes centre-right reformism and revolutionaries who use reforms tactically. Later social democracy (Crosland, the Godesberg Programme) is not read here, and social issues Bernstein does not discuss are left unanswered.
